chunks: Al-Sakuni narrated with his chain of transmission, saying:
The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم said:
"The provision of the traveller is chanting and poetry, so long as there is nothing indecent in it."

key_terms.الْمُسَافِرِ: the traveller or one undertaking a journey
key_terms.زَادُ: provision or sustaining accompaniment for a journey

ai.seo_question: What kind of chanting or poetry is permissible during travel in Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches that chanting and poetry may serve as a fitting accompaniment for travel. Its permissibility is conditioned on being free from indecency and immoral content.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.2447 - Al-Sakuni narrated with his chain of transmission that the Messenger of Allah (swt) (peace and blessings of Allah (swt) be upon him and his family)
"The provision of the traveller is chanting and poetry, as long as it contains nothing immoral."
